newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria schedules delayed council poll for March.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria schedules delayed council poll for March.

text.p: Nigeria's electoral commission NECON on Thursday set March 15 for local council polls that should have been held in December, saying the delay would not affect the rest of the programme to install democracy in October 1998.
"This shift has not affected other parts of the transition programme and we are still very much on course as scheduled," NECON chairman Sumner Dagogo-Jack told a news conference in the capital Abuja.
Politically volatile Nigeria has been hit in recent weeks by a series of bomb blasts targeted at the military in which two soldiers have died and several dozens wounded.
Political sources say they feared the attacks could derail military ruler General Sani Abacha's programme to hand over to an elected president on October 1 next year.
"My worry is the effect the bombs are capable of having on the transition to civil rule programme," said a member of one of the five parties registered by NECON last October to vie for power.
"It could lead to a state of emergency and power cannot be handed over to civilians in chaos," he added.
Africa's most populous nation plunged into crisis in June 1993 when the then military ruler annulled a presidential election to choose his successor.
Moshood Abiola, the undeclared winner of the annulled poll, is in detention for proclaiming himself president and his supporters insist he should be freed and installed president.
Nigeria came under renewed pressure last year to restore democracy when it defied world opinion and hanged nine minority rights activists including writer Ken Saro-Wiwa for murder.
Abacha, who seized power in the chaos of 1993, launched his plan two years later to restore civilian rule, but the opposition and the West have criticised the programme as too long.
His government, however, insists on going ahead with the programme and in March last year it held the first municipal election on a no-party basis.
But other targets like compiling a voters' register were not met and NECON blamed this on the creation of six new states and 183 local council areas last October.
The rescheduled poll would be the first test of the strength of the five political parties.
Dagogo-Jack announced a timetable for other activities such as compilation and production of a voters' register which would begin on February 10 and end on March 7.
He said for the March election there would be 101,151 polling centres in 8,870 wards throughout the 774 municipal areas of the vast West African nation.
There would be no shift of any of the other elements of the transition programme, he said.
These include elections at state levels in the last quarter of this year and a presidential poll between July and September next year.
